questions.context: Suppose that a continuous random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed between $a$ and $b$. The value of mean and variance of $X$ are 9 and 3 respectively.
Suppose that a continuous random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed between $a$ and $b$. The value of mean and variance of $X$ are 9 and 3 respectively.
questions.q: Find the value of $P(5 < X < 7)$. Enter the answer correct to two decimal places.

The number of customers arriving at a bank counter follows a Poisson distribution with an average of 4 arrivals per hour. What is the probability that at least 2 customers arrive in 30 minutes? Enter the answer correct to two decimal places.

The probability mass function of a discrete random variable $X$ is given by

| $X$ | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $P(X = x)$ | 0.2 | $a$ | 0.3 | $b$ |

Find the value of $b$ such that $E(X) = 2.7$. Enter the answer correct to one decimal place.

A random variable $X$ represents the number of packages delivered by a courier company in a day. The cumulative distribution function (CDF) of $X$ is given below:

$$F(x) = \begin{cases} 0 & x < 0 \\ 0.10 & 0 \le x < 1 \\ 0.45 & 1 \le x < 2 \\ 0.70 & 2 \le x < 3 \\ 1 & x \ge 3 \end{cases}$$

Find the value of $P(X > 1 \mid X < 3)$. Enter the answer correct to two decimal places.

questions.q: A box contains 3 red balls and 3 blue balls. A student randomly picks 3 balls without replacement. Let $X$ be the random variable representing the number of red balls selected. Which of the following option is correct?
Consider the dataset 4, 7, 5, 3, 9. If 3 is added to all observations, what is the $75^{\text{th}}$ percentile of the new dataset?

Based on the information given in Table 3, choose the correct option regarding the correlation coefficient $(r)$ between hours studied and test scores of five students.

| Student | Hours Studied | Test Score |
|---|---|---|
| A | 1 | 55 |
| B | 2 | 50 |
| C | 3 | 65 |
| D | 4 | 80 |
| E | 5 | 75 |
options: The value of $r$ is 0.65 and shows a moderate positive correlation.
The value of $r$ is 0.87 and shows a strong positive correlation.
The value of $r$ is 0.92 and shows a very strong positive correlation.
The value of $r$ is $-0.80$ and shows a very strong negative correlation.

questions.q: Which of the following options is(are) correct?
options: The variable height of students is measured on an interval scale.
The average temperature recorded each day for one week is time-series data.
Cross-sectional data are collected at a single point in time across several individuals, firms, or regions etc.
The brand of smartphone a person uses is a qualitative variable.

questions.q:
At a seminar, there are 30 participants, consisting of 20 men and 10 women.

- Each man shakes hands only with other men.
- Each woman shakes hands only with other women.

If every allowed pair of people has exactly one handshake, find the total number of handshakes that occur at the seminar.

There are two bags, Bag A and Bag B. Bag A contains 2 red balls and 1 blue ball, while Bag B contains 1 red ball and 2 blue balls. The probability of choosing Bag A is $1/3$, and the probability of choosing Bag B is $2/3$. After selecting a bag, one ball is drawn from it. What is the probability that the ball drawn is red?
The median of the data set $y_1, y_2, y_3, \dots, y_n$ is $20$. What is the median of the transformed dataset $5y_1 - 3, 5y_2 - 3, 5y_3 - 3, \dots, 5y_n - 3$?
